provider_if_inherited: Cold-chain vendor; smokehouse manufacturer; booking form vendor
implementation_statement: The vendors provide account functions; the owner creates and removes accounts. Each SaaS service has one account, the owner's. Gaps: no account list or periodic review; the laptop's daily account is the administrator account; the smokehouse panel PIN was the factory default until 2026-07-29.
evidence: Account list built in P07; laptop user settings

implementation_statement: Each vendor service enforces access to the owner's tenant. SYS-01 has administrator and view-only roles; only the administrator can change alarm set points and alert contacts.
evidence: SYS-01 role settings; vendor SOC 2 report (P09)

implementation_statement: The owner will create a standard user account on the laptop for daily work and keep the administrator account for installs only, and will give the planned second alert contact a view-only SYS-01 role (2026-10-15).

All remote access to the smokehouse controller and the gateway goes through the vendors' cloud apps; no device has an inbound port open to the internet (router check 2026-07-29). Remote program editing in the smokehouse app was turned off on 2026-08-03; remote monitoring stays on. Gap: remote start and stop remain available to anyone holding the app password.
evidence: Router port check; SYS-02 app settings
regulatory_driver: CSF 2.0 PR.AA-05 (benchmark); 9 CFR 424.21 and 318.6(a) via 303.1(b)(1) (cook and cure integrity)

implementation_statement: No security training so far. The owner will complete a free small-business security course and sign up for monthly reminders by 2026-11-30.

provider_if_inherited: Cold-chain vendor; email and file provider
implementation_statement: SYS-01 logs sign-ins, set point changes, alert contact changes, and acknowledgments. The email provider logs sign-ins. The owner relies on these logs.
evidence: Vendor SOC 2 report (P09); SYS-01 activity log screen

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: Nobody has reviewed the SYS-01 activity log or the email sign-in history. From 2026-09, the owner reviews both on the first Monday of each month (weekly in October to December) and notes the review in the shop log.

Default credentials on the router admin page and the smokehouse panel were changed on 2026-07-29 (P07). Gaps: router firmware never updated; no written list of required settings (alarm set points, alert contacts, offline notice, remote editing off).

The BIA (P05), POL-01 contingency section, and the P08 runbook form the contingency plan, including hourly manual temperature readings. Gaps: no second alert contact, no emergency cooler space agreement, no battery backup for the gateway, and no printed cook programs (due 2026-10-15).
regulatory_driver: CSF 2.0 ID.IM-04 (benchmark); 9 CFR 416.4(d) via 303.1(a)(2)(i) (product protection during storage)

implementation_statement: Vendors back up the data inside their services (temperature history; accounting). Owner responsibility: the custom records spreadsheet, cut sheets, label templates, cure sheet, and cook programs have no backup or version history.
evidence: Vendor SOC 2 report; laptop and file account review

implementation_statement: The owner is the only user of every account and shares no credentials with the slaughter operator, the contractors, or family.

provider_if_inherited: Email and file provider; accounting SaaS vendor; cold-chain vendor
implementation_statement: Every SaaS account is an administrator account. MFA is on for email (text message) and accounting. Gaps: SYS-01 and the booking form admin offer MFA but it is off; the smokehouse app offers none. Owner turns on MFA for SYS-01 and the booking form by 2026-09-15.
evidence: Account security pages; P07 sign-in tests
regulatory_driver: CSF 2.0 PR.AA-03 (benchmark); Fla. Stat. 501.171(2) (booking form data)

implementation_statement: Defaults on the router and smokehouse panel changed 2026-07-29. Gaps: SYS-01 and SYS-02 share one password that was also used for a personal shopping account; passwords are stored in the browser. Plan: password manager with unique passphrases (2026-09-15).
The P08 notification matrix (adopted 2026-08-31) lists who to tell and when. Gap: no security contact registered with the vendors, so vendor breach notices would go to the personal mailbox.
The ransomware runbook (P08) was adopted on 2026-08-31 with a contact list. Gap: contacts not yet printed and the runbook not yet walked through (due 2026-09-30).
No disposal rule. Old paper cut sheets sit in open boxes. POL-01 8.6 sets shredding for paper and a wipe procedure for old devices (2026-12-31).
The shop is locked when the owner is away and the curing agents are in a locked cabinet with the nitrite content marked. Customers stay at the pickup counter.
First risk assessment completed 2026-07-31 using SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01). Reviewed each July and after a major change.

The cold-chain vendor's SOC 2 report was reviewed on 2026-07-30 (P09). Gaps: no vendor list; smokehouse app and AI chatbot terms never read; the chatbot's consumer terms allow use of inputs to improve its service (P10).

The router's firewall blocks inbound connections and the laptop firewall is on. Gaps: one flat network for the laptop, gateway, smokehouse controller, and customers' phones; no guest network. Plan: guest network for customers and a separate network for the two devices (2026-10-15).
Laptop full-disk encryption is on (default) and the phone is encrypted by its passcode. SaaS vendors encrypt stored data (stated in the cold-chain vendor's SOC 2 report; assumed for the others).
evidence: Device encryption status; vendor SOC 2 report

implementation_statement: Automatic updates are on for the laptop and phone; SaaS vendors patch their services. Gaps: the router firmware has never been updated; nobody checks the smokehouse controller and gateway firmware.
The built-in antivirus runs real-time scanning with automatic updates. Owner responsibility: keep it on and act on alerts.
